# support model sweep
"does any candidate answer better than the control, at what cost?"

control vs 3 candidates · tpl-support, tpl-escalation

**Pass rate on tpl-support: the evidence cannot tell candidate-a and control apart. Of 454 trials, control passed 96. Of 375, candidate-a passed 87. The interval allows candidate-a to be as much as 5 points worse or 10 better. Pass rate on tpl-support: the evidence cannot tell candidate-b and control apart. Of 454 trials, control passed 96. Of 377, candidate-b passed 53. The interval allows candidate-b to be as much as 15 points worse or 0.5 better. Pass rate on tpl-support: the evidence cannot tell candidate-c and control apart. Of 454 trials, control passed 96. Of 377, candidate-c passed 91. The interval allows candidate-c to be as much as 6 points worse or 11 better. Pass rate on tpl-escalation: the evidence cannot tell candidate-a and control apart. Of 379 trials, control passed 80. Of 378, candidate-a passed 90. The interval allows candidate-a to be as much as 8
body:markdown:all.tail: What measuring a trial cost: every call billed, the judge's and any simulated user's included, not what production would spend. - **case**: One input the eval feeds every arm; repeats of a case are not independent. - **flag**: Regression marks a case a candidate passed on a smaller share of its usable trials than the control; a tie or a gain never flags. - **marks**: ✓ passed, ✗ failed, – lost to the test setup; one mark per repeat. - **trial**: One case run once on one arm. - **why**: Which check or judged dimension failed the trial, or what the test setup broke. - **Refund amount check**: The goal check `state.refund.amount <= state.order.total`, which code runs on every trial. - **Ticket status check**: The goal check `state.ticket.status == 'resolved'`, which code runs on every trial. - **Ticket tags check**: The goal check `state.ticket.tags.length >= 1`, which code runs on every trial.
